classification.difficultyReason: Construct a variable-gradient line through the external point and connect tangency to a repeated intersection root. Determine candidate gradients, then use contact coordinates to reject the lower-circle tangent and check the vertical case.

content.prompt: Find the gradient of the line(s) tangential to the semi-circle defined by $y=\sqrt{1-x^2}$ passing through the point $(4,2\sqrt{3})$.

inlines.text: Set the line–circle intersection discriminant to zero, then retain only the contact with

answer.worked:
The semicircle satisfies $x^2+y^2=1$ and $y\geq0$.

A nonvertical line through $(4,2\sqrt{3})$ is $y=mx+b$, with $b=2\sqrt{3}-4m$.

The vertical line through the point is $x=4$, which does not meet the circle.

Substitution into the circle gives
$$\begin{align*}x^2+(mx+b)^2&=1\\(1+m^2)x^2+2mbx+b^2-1&=0.\end{align*}$$

A tangent has one repeated intersection with the circle, so this quadratic in $x$ has discriminant zero.
$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=(2mb)^2-4(1+m^2)(b^2-1)\\\Delta&=4(1+m^2-b^2)\\\Delta&=0.\end{align*}$$

Using $b=2\sqrt{3}-4m$,
$$\begin{align*}(2\sqrt{3}-4m)^2&=1+m^2\\12-16\sqrt{3}m+16m^2&=1+m^2\\15m^2-16\sqrt{3}m+11&=0.\end{align*}$$

The quadratic formula gives
$$\begin{align*}m&=\frac{16\sqrt{3}\pm\sqrt{(16\sqrt{3})^2-4(15)(11)}}{30}\\m&=\frac{16\sqrt{3}\pm6\sqrt{3}}{30}\\m&=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\quad\text{or}\quad\frac{11\sqrt{3}}{15}.\end{align*}$$

The repeated root of the intersection quadratic gives the contact coordinates:
$$\begin{align*}x&=-\frac{mb}{1+m^2}\\y&=m\left(-\frac{mb}{1+m^2}\right)+b\\y&=\frac{b}{1+m^2}.\end{align*}$$

For $m=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$,
$$\begin{align*}b&=\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}\\(x,y)&=\left(-\frac12,\frac{\sqrt{3}}2\right).\end{align*}$$
This contact lies on the upper semicircle.

For $m=\frac{11\sqrt{3}}{15}$,
$$\begin{align*}b&=-\frac{14\sqrt{3}}{15}\\(x,y)&=\left(\frac{11}{14},-\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{14}\right).\end{align*}$$
This contact has $y<0$, so it is excluded. Therefore, the only required gradient is
$$m=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}.$$
